Neuroma: The patient presents with pain in the right hand, numbness in the area served by the right median nerve, muscular atrophy in the right forearm, and a fusiform mass at the distal third of the right upper arm. The presence of marked peri- and endoneurial fibrosis, severe axonal loss, and pseudo onion-bulb formations further supports this diagnosis.
Median Nerve Injury: The patient experienced acute severe local pain radiating to his forearm and wrist after a cubital procaine-HCL 0.05% injection, and subsequent numbness, wasting of the thenar muscles, and muscular atrophy in the forearm. The increased distal latency in the median nerve and no response over the thenar muscle on median nerve stimulation at the wrist and elbow also support this diagnosis.
